headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty fell sharply as Indian markets recorded their eighth consecutive weekly loss

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: Persistent selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs)
Global risks and concerns over rising oil prices
Impact of global rate hikes sparking capital outflows
Weakness in global cues and investor caution
whatHappening: Indian benchmark shares posted their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
The Sensex and Nifty extended their losing streak to an eighth consecutive week
In the last session, the Sensex dropped 570.59 points while the Nifty closed at 22,421.95
Approximately Rs 9 lakh crore in investor wealth was wiped out during the market downturn
summary: Indian markets are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti after a volatile session on Thursday where indices extended their losing streak to eight weeks. Persistent FII selling and global economic concerns have resulted in the longest weekly decline for benchmark shares in 25 years. Trading is scheduled to resume on Tuesday, October 6.
